blog.title: Shipping LLM features to production: lessons learned
blog.author: Priya Nair
blog.excerpt: Evaluation, guardrails and cost control are what separate demos from products.
body: Everyone can build an LLM demo in an afternoon. Making it reliable for thousands of users is a different problem.
Start with evaluation: build a test set of real user questions before changing prompts. Add guardrails for input validation and output checks, and track cost per request from day one.
Finally, plan for fallbacks. Models change, APIs fail, and your users should never notice.

blog.title: Cutting Kubernetes costs by 40% without losing reliability
blog.author: Sofia Alvarez
blog.excerpt: Right-sizing, autoscaling and spot capacity: a practical playbook.
body: Most clusters are over-provisioned. Begin by measuring actual CPU and memory usage per workload.
Right-size requests, enable horizontal and cluster autoscaling, and move fault-tolerant jobs to spot instances.
Review monthly. Cost optimisation is a habit, not a project.

blog.title: Why every growing product needs a design system
blog.author: Daniel Kim
blog.excerpt: Consistency, speed and accessibility, all from a shared component library.
body: A design system is more than a style guide: it is shared language between design and engineering.
Teams with a system ship features faster, keep interfaces consistent and make accessibility the default instead of an afterthought.
